title: The extracted modules name their data roots inconsistently
description: The extraction made three __file__-relative paths into injected module-level names, but kept the spike's names: segments uses DATA_ROOT while classify uses DATA and PROMPTS. Renaming was out of scope for a move that forbade renames. For the cleanup bead, alongside the other experiments-inherited debt: render.py's docstring is duplicated across the library half and the CLI half because argparse prints it as --help, and experiments/src/render.py has an unused import sys that predates the move.
acceptance_criteria: The injected roots share one naming convention.

title: Nine stored block files predate the current segments.py
description: 9 of the 181 files in experiments/data/blocks/ do not reproduce under current code, mostly config fw-qwen3.6.whole.v2. They were derived before a segments.py change and never re-derived, so the frozen record is not self-consistent with the frozen code. Found while building the behavioural fingerprint for the extraction, which deliberately pins CURRENT behaviour and is therefore immune. Not urgent and NOT to be fixed by re-deriving casually: rederive.py rewrites those files in place, and experiments/data/test_access.log records a one-shot-per-config held-out budget. Decide whether to re-derive under a recorded run or to annotate the nine as historical.
acceptance_criteria: The nine files either reproduce or are annotated as predating the current code, with the decision recorded in FINDINGS.

title: A stale venv silently fails the wheel test
description: sp-8z5 added setuptools to the dev extras because its wheel test drives the build backend in a subprocess. A venv created before that change does not have it, so the test fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'setuptools' and the suite reads 598 failed / 318 passed rather than 597/319 -- which looks like a code regression and is not one. Hit immediately after merging, on the root venv. uv pip install -e '.[dev]' fixes it. Either the test should skip with a clear reason when the backend is unavailable, or something should detect that the venv predates pyproject's dev extras.
acceptance_criteria: A stale venv produces a message naming the cause, not a failure that reads as a code regression.

title: Nothing links a Recording to the Discovery that found it
description: Discovery stores discovered_count as a number rather than being derivable from the Recordings it produced, because no scenario asks which Discovery found a given Recording. The consequence: if a count is ever written wrong it cannot be re-derived, and the count is what system_health.feature:27 shows the operator. Worth a link if anything later needs to audit the number, or an explicit note that the count is authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: Either a Recording names the Discovery that found it, or DOMAIN.md states that discovered_count is authoritative and why.

title: Health-view dependency statuses are a live probe, not stored state
description: system_health.feature:12-19 and :44-49 show the object store, job queue, transcription service, disk, ffmpeg and notification channel with health statuses, and the Degraded scenario probes live and names the unhealthy dependency. Read that way they are a probe rather than rows, which is why the Discovery work deliberately did not model them. Recorded so a later reading does not mistake the omission for an oversight -- if those statuses must be durable (for history or trend), that is a new gap this bead did not close.
acceptance_criteria: Either the statuses are confirmed as probe-only in DOMAIN.md, or the durable ones are modelled.

title: Recording.skip_reason may no longer have a scenario of its own
description: The SkippedObject entity now holds why an object was never ingested -- keyed on the object key, because three of the four skip reasons describe keys no Recording row can exist for. That was skip_reason's stated purpose ('why an object was not ingested at all', DOMAIN.md:60), so the field may now be orphaned, which violates the standing rule that a field with no scenario behind it does not get built. It survives for now because recording_download.feature:68 and recording_detail.feature:56 want a Recording-level failure reason, which is a different thing and is owned by other beads. Decide its fate alongside those: either cite the behaviour that still forces it, or remove it.
acceptance_criteria: skip_reason either cites a scenario that forces it or is removed.

title: NEW ENTITY: retained accuracy-suite results
description: detection_accuracy.feature:106,:244 'When the accuracy suite runs before and after / Then the change in median and worst-case error is reported'. Needs per-run, per-pair errors plus aggregates keyed on the configuration measured. Arguable: may belong to the experiments harness and its test_access.log rather than the application model -- but something must retain a before to compare an after against.
acceptance_criteria: Suite runs are retained per configuration so a before/after comparison is possible.

title: Log entries must be written at stage start, not only completion
description: recording_detail.feature:44 'Then I see which analysis stage is currently running / And I see which stages have completed', and approval.feature:40-41 'the current processing step' and 'an indication of progress'. Completed stages derive from completion entries; a currently-running stage and any progress indication do not. Refines the per-stage naming bead: the entry must exist at start.
acceptance_criteria: A running stage is visible from the log without waiting for it to finish.

title: Transcript text is not searchable
description: recording_list.feature:88 'And I can search by date, by classification, and by what was said'. Label and summary search are covered by Segment.label and Block.summary; 'what was said' needs transcript text queryable rather than an opaque artifact path. The scenario's own comment concedes 'this list has no search' yet it is tagged @happy-path @measured rather than @deferred -- resolve the tension either way.
acceptance_criteria: Either transcript text is searchable, or the scenario is retagged to match what v1 does.

title: Artifact path fields assume the file still exists
description: storage_and_retention.feature:38 'Then only the current MP3 is stored / And the settings needed to reproduce the previous one are retained'. entities.py makes path, size_bytes and checksum non-optional, which encodes 'the file exists', where Recording.local_path was deliberately made nullable for exactly this case. Arguable: file-gone is derivable from superseded_by being non-null.
acceptance_criteria: A superseded render whose file is gone is representable without a misleading path.

title: A render waiting for disk has no waiting_since
description: processing_orchestration.feature:90 'Then processing does not begin / And the Segment stays in approved pending space / And a storage alert is raised'. Derivable from state approved plus a queued render Job, and no scenario asks for oldest-first retry here -- which is the only reason Recording.waiting_since exists. Noted for symmetry, not urgency.
acceptance_criteria: Either a Segment records when it began waiting for space, or DOMAIN.md states why the Recording analogue is not needed.

title: Recording does not store its probed codec
description: audio_probe.feature:14 lists 'codec | flac' among probe outputs and recording_download.feature:29 lists 'format | flac'. Arguable: constant across all 85 objects today and recoverable from the key's extension, so it may be deliberately omitted -- but it is asserted as recorded.
acceptance_criteria: Either the codec is stored, or DOMAIN.md says why it is not.
close_reason: Decided NOT to store the probed codec: the object key already names it and README records container/codec as a project-wide constant. Pinned by a test that fails if anyone adds the field, and the decision is recorded in DOMAIN.md so it reads as considered rather than overlooked.

title: Retried job eligibility requires a join to the log
description: job_queue.feature:35 'Then it is retried with increasing delay between attempts'. Derivable from attempts plus the last attempt's LogEntry.occurred_at, so not a gap by the rules -- but queue eligibility then means joining the log on every poll. A next_attempt_at on Job would make the queue a single indexed query.
acceptance_criteria: Queue eligibility is answerable without joining the processing log.

title: Two waveform_peaks artifacts for one Recording are indistinguishable
description: waveform_generation.feature:24 'Then peak data is available at an overview resolution covering the whole recording / And at a detail resolution suitable for placing a boundary within 100 ms'. If both are stored they are two artifacts of the same kind with nothing to tell them apart -- render_settings and asr_config are kind-specific and peaks have no equivalent. Arguable: the detail level could be generated on demand from the envelope, once the envelope is storable.
acceptance_criteria: Either peak artifacts carry their resolution, or the detail level is generated on demand by a stated decision.

title: An artifact cannot tell whether its source was replaced
description: preview_audio.feature:91 'Given the source was re-downloaded / Then the preview is regenerated / And no reviewer ever hears audio from a different Recording'. Arguable because it is satisfiable behaviourally by invalidating every derived artifact on re-download -- but nothing records which source version an artifact derives from, so the guarantee rests on remembering to invalidate.
acceptance_criteria: Staleness after a re-download is prevented by a mechanism that does not rely on remembering.

title: A suggested publication label cannot be distinguished from a written one
description: summarization.feature:42 'Then Hebrews 12 is suggested as the publication label / And the reviewer can correct it', and publication_details.feature:49 'Then the label is suggested as Hebrews 12'. A suggestion cannot simply be written into label, because approval.feature:77 depends on 'no publication label has been entered' being true until a human types one. Either a separate suggestion field, or a written-by-human marker.
acceptance_criteria: A suggested label and a human-written label are distinguishable, and approval still knows when none was entered.

title: Silence gaps are required for boundary snapping and may not be stored
description: blocking.feature:105 'Then every silence gap longer than 2 seconds is recorded with its start and end / And those gaps are available for snapping a boundary later', :94 'And the silence is recorded as a pause within the Block', transcription.feature:42. Arguable only because the gaps may live inside the transcript artifact's file -- nothing says so, and the envelope they would otherwise be recomputed from is itself unstorable until the envelope artifact kind exists. If the transcript file is not the intended home this becomes certain.
acceptance_criteria: Silence gaps are persisted somewhere the snapping code can read them.

title: Diarization speaker labels and multi-speaker Blocks are not stored
description: blocking.feature:58 'And every Block has a start time, an end time and a speaker label', :126 'And the Block records that it contains multiple speakers', :137/:145 'And each Block is marked as having no speaker attribution'. speaker_matches[] holds only enrolled-profile similarities, so a generic cluster label like Speaker 3 has nowhere to go. Arguable: derivable from the diarization artifact by span overlap, and no-attribution from that artifact's absence -- decide whether the artifact file is the intended home.
acceptance_criteria: A Block's speaker label, multi-speaker marker and no-attribution state are reachable by a decided route.

title: Nothing flags a Block as possibly two types
description: block_classification.feature:376 'Then the Block is flagged as possibly containing more than one type / And the reviewer can split it'. evidence[] is free text about findings; nothing holds the assertion itself the way retyped_by_human holds its assertion, so the split affordance has nothing to key on.
acceptance_criteria: A Block can be flagged as possibly multi-type, and that flag drives the split affordance.
close_reason: Block.possibly_multiple_types, which the reviewer's split affordance needs something to key on; evidence[] is free text and cannot carry the assertion.

title: Recording has no one-line summary of what it was
description: block_classification.feature:291 'And the Recording is summarised as <event> rather than as other', with examples 'a Good Friday service' and 'a Saturday worship and prayer gathering'. kind is a seven-value enum that cannot carry the event, Block has summary, Recording has nothing. Distinct from the derivable headlines in analysis_confidence.feature:197,:206.
acceptance_criteria: Recording carries a one-line summary of what the service was.

title: A vocabulary test restates its own definition
description: tests/test_store_vocabularies.py asserts LOGGED_STATES == RECORDING_STATES + SEGMENT_STATES, which is verbatim the definition in vocabularies.py -- a tautology that pins nothing and cannot fail. The behaviour its name claims is genuinely covered elsewhere, by the CLOSED_COLUMNS entry driving the accept-every-declared-value test against the real database, so coverage is fine; the test is just weaker than its name.
acceptance_criteria: The test asserts behaviour rather than restating the definition, or it is removed as redundant.

title: A Segment state can be logged without naming the Segment
description: DOMAIN.md says of LogEntry that 'segment_id says whose', but entered_state='approved' with segment_id NULL stores fine, asserting a Segment state for a Recording. Low impact precisely because the two lifecycles are disjoint, so entered_state alone is self-describing and any contradiction is detectable rather than corrupting -- which also makes segment_id redundant for the disambiguation that row credits it with.
acceptance_criteria: A logged Segment state names its Segment, or the row stops claiming that it does.

title: NOT NULL TEXT columns accept empty and whitespace
description: LogEntry.correlation_id is NOT NULL on the stated argument that 'an identifier that may be absent is the same as no identifier', but empty string and whitespace both store, so the invariant is half-enforced. This is project-wide for every NOT NULL TEXT column, not a regression in the log -- but correlation_id's row states the stronger claim, and system_health.feature:61 depends on the value actually correlating to something.
acceptance_criteria: A NOT NULL TEXT column that states a non-empty invariant enforces it.

title: LogEntry allows nonsense column combinations
description: One log table with an open kind means no constraint says which column combinations are legal. Stored freely: a human action with a duration_seconds, a job attempt with an actor, an error with no job_id, a negative duration, punch_out before punch_in, a boundary set with no approver, kind='', and an entry with no subject, state or relation at all. Consistent with the rest of the model -- Artifact likewise never ties render_settings or segment_id to its kind -- and it matters little at 39 recordings and roughly one a week. The schema's closed= primitive is per-column, so cross-column CHECKs need a new primitive. Worth doing when that primitive exists; meanwhile DOMAIN.md should not imply the shape is self-policing.
acceptance_criteria: Either cross-column constraints exist, or DOMAIN.md states plainly that entry shape is a caller responsibility.

title: No field names which analysis stage a log entry belongs to
description: interface/recording_detail.feature:46-48 requires showing which analysis stage is currently running and which have completed. analysis_orchestration.feature names twelve stages in order (envelope, probe, waveform, preview, transcription, diarization, blocking, block_classification, summarization, segment_proposal, boundary_refinement, scoring). Job.kind is 'analyze', not per-stage, and LogEntry.kind is an open set -- so this is expressible by convention but nothing names a stage or closes the set. Worth deciding before the interface depends on a convention nothing enforces.
acceptance_criteria: A log entry identifies its analysis stage in a way the interface can rely on.

title: A Recording's failure reason is derivable but has no direct home
description: interface/recording_detail.feature:55 has a Recording in analysis_failed 'with reason transcription timed out' and requires 'I see the failure reason'. With the processing log in place this is now derivable -- the entry entering analysis_failed, or the last failed attempt's error -- where before it was not holdable at all. LogEntry.error is documented as attempt-scoped, so reading a Recording's current failure means a query rather than a field. Decide whether that is good enough or whether Recording.failure_reason should exist; do not add it without deciding, since a stored copy would be a second source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: The failure reason is reachable for the detail view, by a decided route.

title: The count drift test's coverage is hand-maintained
description: COUNTED_SETS in tests/test_store_vocabularies.py is a hand-maintained two-entry list. It covers both DOMAIN.md rows that state a count today and it does bite in both directions, but a future field row stating a count is unguarded -- the same hand-maintenance drift that sp-382 existed to catch. SPEC_VOCABULARIES already enumerates every closed set, so the check could derive its own coverage instead of listing it.
acceptance_criteria: Every DOMAIN.md row stating a count is checked without a hand-maintained list.

title: Two new DOMAIN.md rows are paragraph-length
description: The domain-alignment batch added table rows of 300-598 characters where the file's longest pre-existing row was 278. DOMAIN.md:83 (598 chars) and :127 (509) are paragraph-length essays inside a table cell. The convention is a citation in one or two terse sentences; rationale that needs more room belongs in ARCHITECTURE.md.
acceptance_criteria: Field rows carry a terse citation; longer reasoning lives where rationale belongs.

title: The processing log is filed as undecided when it is known debt
description: DOMAIN.md:219 lists the processing log under 'What this model deliberately does not decide', but its own text says it is 'an entity the spec requires and this model does not have'. Every other bullet in that section is a genuinely open option (hard delete, whether a second analysis runs, whether local audio is reclaimed). features/AUDIT.md is this project's existing home for 'the spec asks for X and X does not exist'. The disclosure is honest and its four citations check out verbatim; only the heading mislabels it -- which matters because a debt parked among decisions is how the Notification entity stayed missing.
acceptance_criteria: Known spec debt lives in AUDIT.md, and the does-not-decide section holds only genuinely open questions.

title: Speaker similarity is unbounded and duplicate voice links are allowed
description: SpeakerMatch.similarity accepts and round-trips -0.5, 1.5, 42.0, inf and -inf; NaN is refused only incidentally, by SQLite coercing it to NULL against the NOT NULL. Duplicate speaker_profile_ids on one Block are also accepted. No scenario bounds either value, and peer floats (self_reported_confidence, active_fraction) carry no CHECK, so this is consistent with the model rather than wrong -- noted because this number feeds 'and how confidently' on the reviewer's screen, where a similarity of 42 would be nonsense.
acceptance_criteria: similarity is bounded to the range the measurement produces, and a voice links to a Block once.

title: Proposal supersession allows cycles, self-supersession and cross-Segment links
description: superseded_by is unconstrained beyond its foreign key. Verified accepted: self-supersession (p.superseded_by = p.proposal_id), a two-node cycle (a->b, b->a), and supersession by a Proposal belonging to a different Segment. Each makes lists(Proposal, segment_id=..., superseded_by=None) return nothing for a Segment that has Proposals -- and DOMAIN.md:127 says which Proposal is current 'has to be a stored fact'. Artifact.superseded_by has the identical hole, so the cited precedent is followed faithfully; worth closing now that supersession answers a question the spec asks.
acceptance_criteria: A Proposal cannot supersede itself, form a cycle, or supersede one belonging to another Segment.

title: A mis-keyed Collection.references silently drops the foreign key
description: Collection.references became a per-column dict to carry the SpeakerMatch FK. A typo in a key (references={'profiel_id': ...}) emits DDL with no REFERENCES clause and no error. Table.references and Table.closed behave the same way, so this is not a new class of defect -- but the old single-string form made a collection's FK impossible to mis-key, and nothing tests it. A one-line assertion that every references key is an element column would close it.
acceptance_criteria: A references key that names no column fails loudly.

title: Path resolution collapses .. textually rather than resolving it
description: artifact_paths.py uses os.path.normpath, so 'link/../secret.txt' where link is a symlink out of the data root is rewritten to root/secret.txt instead of being resolved POSIX-style. The result is safely inside the root -- it just names a different file than the caller wrote. Separately, a path containing a NUL byte raises a bare ValueError from lstat rather than PathEscapesDataRoot; both are ValueError, so a caller catching the base class is unaffected. Found while attacking the guard with 25 inputs, all of which stayed inside the root.
acceptance_criteria: Path resolution matches POSIX semantics, and every refusal raises the store's own error type.

title: A stale database schema is silently accepted
description: opens_store executescripts CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so an existing database with an older schema is accepted and then fails later with an OperationalError at the first query touching a new column. Omitting a migration framework is right at 39 recordings and ~1/week, but the silence could be made loud with a schema-hash check at open.
acceptance_criteria: A database whose schema does not match the code is reported at open, not at first query.

title: Store helper names depart from the naming rule
description: close() is the one Store method that is not a third-person singular verb phrase, alongside saves/loads/lists/resolves. Several module helpers are noun phrases too: order_by, to_column, from_column, values_of, column_names. CONVENTIONS.md keeps LS-003's naming rule even though the Rails-scoped ADR itself does not apply here.
acceptance_criteria: Names are third-person singular verb phrases.

title: A NaN in a REAL column silently becomes 'not measured'
description: float('nan') stored in a REAL column comes back as None, turning 'measured and degenerate' into 'never measured'. This matters for the emptiness-gate fields dynamic_range_db, active_fraction and longest_active_seconds, where that distinction decides whether a recording is treated as empty.
acceptance_criteria: A degenerate measurement is distinguishable from an absent one.

title: The store has no single-row sanity constraints
description: Accepted without complaint: Block(start=500, end=10), Segment(punch_in=900, punch_out=10), negative timecodes, Job(attempts=-5, max_attempts=0), an Artifact whose superseded_by is itself, and a Segment on recording r2 seeded by a Block belonging to r1. Multi-row block contiguity genuinely cannot be a CHECK, but every case above can. Deliberately out of scope for sp-1vn.3, whose criteria named only the closed sets.
acceptance_criteria: Single-row invariants a CHECK can express are enforced.
notes: Also in this class, added after the sp-1i8 span work (2026-09-19): punch points must fall inside the Segment's own span (span_start_seconds <= punch_in_seconds, punch_out_seconds <= span_end_seconds). sp-1i8 deliberately did NOT add that CHECK, on the grounds that the store asserts no single-row invariants at all today and adding one alone would be inconsistent — so it belongs here, with the rest. Verified accepted today: a span whose end precedes its start, a negative span, a zero-length span, a span narrower than its own punch points, 9e9 and +/-inf. Also in this class: ChannelLevel allows duplicate channel numbers, channel 0, channel -7, and eight levels on a two-channel Recording.

title: The DDL generator does not escape SQL string literals
description: quoted() in src/sermon/store/schema.py emits 'it''s' incorrectly as 'it's' for a value containing an apostrophe. Unexploitable today -- no vocabulary value contains one, and all 12 sets are derived from the spec's own tables -- but the generator has no defence if one ever does.
acceptance_criteria: Values are escaped, or a value that cannot be safely quoted fails loudly.

title: Collection links silently keep duplicates
description: Link tables key on (owner, position), so enrolled_from=('r1','r1') round-trips unchanged and one speaker_profile_id can be linked to the same block twice. DOMAIN.md:165 describes enrolled_from as 'Which Recordings contributed. Needed to un-enrol', which reads as a set.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate links are refused or deduplicated, per what the spec implies.

title: The speaker N:M link is navigable in only one direction
description: DOMAIN.md:32 draws SpeakerProfile -> Block, but lists(Block, speaker_profile_ids=...) and lists(SpeakerProfile, enrolled_from=...) both raise ValueError because column_names() excludes collection fields. The link round-trips from the Block side, so the relationship exists, but profile -> blocks needs raw SQL. segment_review.feature asks which enrolled voice is teaching (the Block-side question); the reverse direction is what un-enrolling a speaker needs.
acceptance_criteria: Both directions of the link are queryable through the store.

title: DOMAIN.md writes Block evidence as a scalar but the spec asserts several
description: DOMAIN.md:78 writes Block's evidence unbracketed while DOMAIN.md:118 writes Proposal's as evidence[]. analysis/block_classification.feature:165-166 asserts two evidence entries on a single Block ('sustained single-speaker teaching' AND 'follows a scripture reading') and :90 says each Block carries the evidence that produced it -- so the plural is correct and DOMAIN.md's wording misleads. The store was changed to an ordered child table under sp-1vn.3; this is the documentation half.
acceptance_criteria: DOMAIN.md writes Block evidence as a collection.

title: Job.job_id is the one surrogate id no scenario forces
description: Job.job_id was added as a row identity, but nothing in DOMAIN.md references a job identity -- unlike seed_block_id, segment_id, superseded_by and speaker_profile_id, which the N:M link needs. dedupe_key is already UNIQUE and could serve. Defensible as a row identity, but it is the one addition the sp-1vn.3 rule 'a field with no scenario behind it does not get built' does not cover.
acceptance_criteria: Either a forcing behaviour is cited for job_id, or it is removed.

title: Recording.kind is nullable while the vocabulary already has 'unknown'
description: RECORDING_KINDS contains 'unknown' (README.md:96) and Recording.kind is also nullable, so there are two encodings of one fact. DOMAIN.md:53 flags no nullability for the field. Pick one.
acceptance_criteria: A recording of unknown kind has exactly one representation.

title: Source-no-longer-available flags have no fields
description: operations/storage_and_retention.feature requires that a Recording can be flagged 'source no longer available' and that its skipped Segments are marked as no longer extractable. DOMAIN.md has no field for either. Related but distinct from the open Q34 question about whether local audio is ever reclaimed, which DOMAIN.md does list as deliberately undecided.
acceptance_criteria: Both flags exist in DOMAIN.md and the store, or the scenarios are changed.
close_reason: source no longer available is a Recording warning, and the Segment side is a query over it rather than a second flag. No state transition accompanies it — a reviewed Recording stays reviewed, which the scenario implies by naming no transition.

title: validate_spec docstring names the out-of-range interpreter
description: features/validate_spec.py:9 still says to run it from features/ as 'python3 validate_spec.py'. python3 on PATH is 3.14.3, outside the >=3.13,<3.14 pyproject declares, and that command exits 2 with 'gherkin-official is not installed'. CLAUDE.md was corrected to .venv/bin/python features/validate_spec.py; this docstring now contradicts it. The script itself is cwd-independent (Path(__file__).parent), so the instruction is merely stale.
acceptance_criteria: The docstring names a command that runs.

title: Size test spawns a redundant collect-only subprocess
description: tests/test_spec_harness.py:76 test_the_spec_is_the_size_this_harness_was_built_for runs a --collect-only subprocess identical to the one test_the_spec_module_collects_every_declared_scenario already runs. Harmless at this size; the count could be shared through a session fixture.
acceptance_criteria: The collection count is obtained once per session.

title: A step module's plural name describes a single-module operation
description: tests/conftest.py:11 loads_step_definitions loads and returns exactly one module from one path; the plural reads as the whole-directory operation, which is pytest_configure. loads_step_module or loads_step_definitions_from would match. The third-person singular verb form is already correct per CONVENTIONS.md.
acceptance_criteria: The name describes what the function does.

title: features/README declares two tags no scenario uses
description: The tag table in features/README.md declares @needs-decision and @mobile, which no scenario carries. validate_spec.py enforces the dangerous direction only (every tag used must be declared), so this passes. @needs-decision is expected to be empty -- all spec decisions are settled -- but @mobile is suspicious: interface/segment_review.feature has a Rule about mobile review that carries no such tag. Decide whether the tag or the table is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Either the tags are used, or they are removed from the table, with the mobile scenarios' tagging decided deliberately.

title: gherkin-official floods every run with 4040 DeprecationWarnings
description: A full suite run emits ~4040 DeprecationWarnings from inside gherkin-official==29.0.0 (gherkin_line.py:79, maxsplit passed positionally). 808 arise from pytest-bdd's own parse, so they appear on every run regardless of the harness tests. Harmless, but they bury any real warning, which matters because the harness relies on warnings-as-errors to catch unknown marks. No filter was added in sp-1vn.2 deliberately, to avoid masking anything.
acceptance_criteria: A clean run's warning output is readable: the dependency is bumped, or the warning is filtered narrowly enough that a new warning from our own code still surfaces.

title: Nothing tests that the spec guardrail still detects anything
description: Neutering validate_spec.main() to return 0 leaves all harness tests green: the guardrail is wired in, but its ability to detect a regression is untested. It is demonstrably live today -- planting forbidden implementation vocabulary in a scenario and adding an undeclared tag each fail the suite -- so this is a latent hole rather than a present one.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails if validate_spec stops detecting a known-bad spec.

title: Spec roots and marker descriptions are duplicated
description: PROJECT_ROOT/SPEC_ROOT are defined three times (tests/test_spec_harness.py:9, tests/conftest.py:6, tests/test_spec.py:5). Separately, the 17 marker descriptions in pyproject.toml duplicate features/README.md's table prose while the test compares only names, so the descriptions can drift from the table unnoticed.
acceptance_criteria: The roots have one definition; either the descriptions are compared too or they stop being duplicated.

title: Six scenario names collide across feature files
description: Collecting all 604 scenarios in one module collapses six duplicate scenario names to _1 suffixes -- e.g. 'A quiet margin around the cut' in analysis/punch_in_detection.feature:39 and analysis/punch_out_detection.feature:76, and 'Both channels carry signal' in analysis/audio_probe.feature:40 and processing/audio_rendering.feature:30. No scenario is lost (604 == 604) and the suffix survived a file rename, but test_a_quiet_margin_around_the_cut_1 no longer says which feature file it came from, and a step definition written for punch-in will be matched against punch-out. The collision is in features/; renaming scenarios is a spec edit and must keep validate_spec.py passing.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario names are unique across the spec, or node ids carry their feature file.

title: Deferred-tag hook reimplements pytest-bdd's own default
description: tests/conftest.py:23 applies pytest.mark.deferred(function) and discards the return value, relying on in-place mutation. It duplicates what pytest-bdd's default pytest_bdd_apply_tag already does. Applying only skip and returning None lets the default apply the mark, and is shorter.
acceptance_criteria: The hook applies only what pytest-bdd does not, and does not rely on a discarded return value.

title: Harness helpers are noun phrases, against LS-003 naming
description: CONVENTIONS.md LS-003 keeps the naming rule: one operation per unit, named as a third-person singular verb phrase. In tests/test_spec_harness.py, runs_pytest complies; counted (:24), tag_names (:30), expanded_scenarios (:34) and declared_scenarios (:49) do not. Four against one in a 110-line file.
acceptance_criteria: Helper names are third-person singular verb phrases.

title: Marker registration is asserted from pyproject, not from effective pytest config
description: tests/test_spec_harness.py:80 reads pyproject.toml's file content via tomllib rather than pytest's resolved configuration. Adding a pytest.ini shadowed all 17 marker registrations, producing 15 PytestUnknownMarkWarning, and this test still passed. Only test_no_tag_the_spec_uses_is_an_unknown_mark caught it, and that one structurally cannot cover the two declared-but-unused tags (@mobile, @needs-decision).
acceptance_criteria: The test reads pytest's effective markers so a shadowing config file fails the suite.

title: Harness test discards a return code it should check
description: tests/test_spec_harness.py:64 calls runs_pytest(...)[1] and throws away the second run's return code, so the expected total is computed from an unchecked baseline. The primary run's returncode still catches a collection error, so this is cosmetic rather than a live hole.
acceptance_criteria: Both return codes are checked, or the second run is removed.

title: Decompose Operations and notifications into per-Rule beads
description: features/operations + features/notifications — 43 scenarios. The Job table and worker, health view, retention, approval notifications.
acceptance_criteria: Every non-@deferred Rule in the phase has exactly one bead, or is listed as needing none with a stated reason. Every bead: acceptance criteria drawn from its own scenarios rather than invented; named governing feature file and Rule; dependencies only within this phase or on closed work. Cross-cutting concepts are named and handled deliberately rather than sliced per-Rule. bd ready after the change offers only beads whose dependencies are genuinely satisfiable.

title: Widen import-hygiene scanning beyond src/
description: The hygiene tests cover src/ only. Step definitions land in tests/steps/ and services/ exists; a step definition importing experiments code is currently unchecked.
acceptance_criteria: tests/ and services/ are scanned by the same assertions that cover src/.

title: Pin pytest; it is the one floating dev dependency
description: pytest-bdd and playwright are pinned to the versions ARCHITECTURE.md calls verified; pytest is not, so it resolves to whatever is current (9.1.1 today). The '604 tests collect' claim therefore rests on a floating runner.
acceptance_criteria: pytest is pinned; the suite still collects 604 tests.

title: Clean comments to the LS-004 bar, separately
description:
Dedicated commit after the move is proved identical, never combined with it — ADR-LS-004 section 7.

Outstanding on adoption: 18 comment blocks over the three-line ceiling, 9 carrying dates, 5 first person, 5.5% density. Most duplicate FINDINGS, which is where rationale belongs.
acceptance_criteria: No comment block exceeds three lines; no dates, first person, or narrative voice in code comments; behaviour provably unchanged again.

title: Deploy to nas
description: Homelab stack following the workouts precedent, Caddy route, ZFS dataset, Garage secrets. Includes the first end-to-end run on the real box, which every performance claim is still conditional on.
notes: Children not yet created. Decompose one bead per Rule: in the governing feature files when this phase starts — a Rule is 2-5 scenarios and a natural Red-Green unit. Deliberately not generated up front: the first two phases will reshape what these look like, and 130 mechanically-titled beads would be worse than none.
